# Transition III: The Widening World

The first thing Bob noticed about Michigan State was the smell of it — a composite odor of old brick and cut grass and the particular staleness of buildings where thousands of people breathed the same air for months at a time. He had arrived in September, carrying a cardboard box of possessions and wearing the expression of a boy who was trying very hard to look like he belonged. He was seventeen, a freshman in the truest sense: new to everything, uncertain
